outcome: No result found that settles the original Browkin-Brzeziński n-conjecture (setwise-coprime n-tuples, no vanishing proper subsum) or any case/restriction of it as stated in the Wikipedia bullet. All 2024-2026 activity found concerns the 'strong n-conjecture', a related but distinct variant (Vojta 1998 / Ramaekers 2009) that replaces setwise coprimality with pairwise coprimality, which is a change of hypothesis rather than a restriction of the original statement.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet describes the original Browkin-Brzeziński (1994) n-conjecture: n>=3 integers that are coprime as a set (gcd of all n = 1), sum to zero, and have no vanishing proper subsum, satisfy an inequality (equivalently, quality limsup = 2n-5). Two lines of 2024-2026 activity were found, and both concern a different, stronger conjecture, not this one. (1) Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan, 'Improved lower bounds for strong n-conjectures' (arXiv:2409.13439, first posted 2024-09-20, journal version Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society, online 2025-06-02) prove lower bounds of 5/4 (n>=6) and 5/3 (odd n>=5) on the quality limsup for the 'strong n-conjecture' -- Vojta's 1998 variant requiring PAIRWISE coprimality of the n-tuple, with Ramaekers' (2009 thesis) further restriction that the limsup equals exactly 1. Their bounds disprove Ramaekers' conjecture for n>=5, but say nothing about the original Browkin-Brzeziński statement, which the paper itself explicitly distinguishes (their Definition 1.8/1.9 vs. the original setwise condition). I fetched the arXiv HTML (v2) and confirmed: acknowledgements thank Benne de Weger for correspondence and the referee for proofreading -- no computational or AI tool is mentioned anywhere in the paper; the proof method is polynomial identities (building on Darmon-Granville and Elkies) and Pell equations, entirely by hand. (2) Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan (or a related author set), 'Strong n-conjectures over rings of integers' (arXiv:2503.05296, posted 2025-03-07) extends the same strong/Ramaekers variant to Gaussian integers and Hurwitz quaternions -- again explicitly the strong variant, and again no AI or computational tool disclosed in the acknowledgements (only a Singapore MOE funding acknowledgement for F. Stephan). Neither paper is a restriction (case) of the original n-conjecture in the sense of Section 3.1: pairwise coprimality is a strictly stronger hypothesis than setwise coprimality, so a pairwise-coprime n-tuple is a special case of a setwise-coprime one, meaning the strong n-conjecture's truth or falsity constrains a strict subset of the tuples the original conjecture ranges over -- but the two papers' RESULTS (lower bounds on quality, disproof of Ramaekers) do not translate into any statement about the original conjecture's own inequality (2n-5), because the original conjecture is about a strictly larger, differently-shaped search space and its own best known quality bound is unaffected. This is why I classify it as a related/distinct problem rather than a settled case: the Wikipedia bullet's own numerical claim (limsup = 2n-5) is untouched by these results. Additionally, on 2026-09-22 I found a September 2026 entry on Wikipedia's 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence' describing a Lean counterexample to 'the n=4 case of the N conjecture' by Tom Adamczewski (Epoch AI) using an unreleased OpenAI model referred to as 'GPT-6 Astra'. I traced this to its primary source, github.com/tadamcz/n-conjecture-strong, whose README states verbatim: 'A standalone Lean proof refuting the n = 4 case of the strong n-conjecture as stated in Hölzl-Kleine-Stephan, Conjecture 7' -- i.e. this AI-generated result is explicitly about the STRONG n-conjecture (the Ramaekers/Hölzl-Kleine-Stephan variant), not the original Browkin-Brzeziński n-conjecture of the Wikipedia bullet; the Wikipedia AI-discoveries list's shorthand 'N conjecture' is imprecise relative to its own linked primary source. The repo's own text states the entire repository, including the Lean proof, was machine-written by GPT-6 Astra at Adamczewski's direction -- this would be ai_role 'generated' if it were in scope, but because the object of the proof is the strong (pairwise-coprime) variant and not the conjecture as stated in this bullet, it is out of scope under Section 3.1 and I have not credited it to this record. I searched extensively for any work on the original setwise-coprime n-conjecture itself (by name, by the Browkin-Brzeziński names, and by the abc-conjecture-generalization framing) and found none since January 2024; all located activity is on the strong/pairwise variant.
competing_reading: One could argue that because pairwise coprimality implies setwise coprimality, every pairwise-coprime tuple counted by the strong n-conjecture is also counted by the original n-conjecture, so disproving Ramaekers' conjecture (a claim about the limsup over pairwise-coprime tuples) at least demonstrates large-quality examples that also lie within the original conjecture's domain, which could be read as 'progress' bearing on the original bound. Against this: the original n-conjecture's own claimed bound is 2n-5, far above the 5/3 or 5/4 lower bounds established, so these examples do not threaten or move the original conjecture's stated inequality, and the papers make no claim to. I judge the 'related problem, not a case with bearing on this bullet's own numerical content' reading as the stronger one, consistent with the triage's own uncertainty and with Section 3.1's instruction that a changed hypothesis (pairwise vs setwise) is a variant, not a restriction, when the settled result does not narrow the original bullet's own claim.
what_would_settle_it: A published result stating a bound, case, or disproof specifically for the original Browkin-Brzeziński n-conjecture's setwise-coprime, no-vanishing-proper-subsum formulation (i.e. explicitly relaxing pairwise to setwise coprimality), or an explicit statement by Hölzl-Kleine-Stephan or another author connecting their strong-n-conjecture bounds back to the original conjecture's 2n-5 claim.
